title: 5.1.23 Sprite Playground
description: Build a sprite playground combining canvas, a keyboard-controlled sprite (WASD or arrow keys), auto-motion, and on-screen text. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create a canvas and two sprites
steps.instructions: Make a canvas (any size between 300×300 and 800×600) and two sprites: one `player` (controllable) and one `mover` (moves on its own).

steps.title: Wire keyboard movement to the player
steps.instructions: Use `kb.pressing(...)` with `'a'` / `'d'` / `'w'` / `'s'` (or `'left'` / `'right'` / `'up'` / `'down'`) to set the player's velocity. Include an else branch that resets velocity to 0 when no key is held.
hints: Pick one set of keys and use it for all four directions. 5.1.14 lists both sets, and 5.1.17 explains the else branch.

steps.title: Animate the mover sprite
steps.instructions: Make the `mover` sprite move on its own, with no key held. One way is the one 5.1.22 shows: work its position out from `frameCount`, such as `sin(frameCount * 0.05)` to swing it back and forth, or turn it with `rotation` to spin it. A simpler way counts too: add a little to its position every frame, like `mover.pos.x = mover.pos.x + 1;` from 5.1.9, or give it a velocity once in `setup()`, as in 5.1.15.
hints: 5.1.22 shows swinging, circling and spinning with `frameCount`, and the simpler ways, each with a line you can copy.
Run it and keep your hands off the keys. The mover should still move.

steps.title: Add an on-screen text label
steps.instructions: Display a message on the canvas using `fill()`, `textSize()` and `text()`. Your choice of message.
hints: 5.1.21 shows all three. Call `fill('white')` before `text(...)` so the words show up on a dark background.

steps.title: Clear the background each frame
steps.instructions: Make sure `background(...)` is called each frame so previous frames don't stack up.

requirements.title: Create a canvas
requirements.description: A canvas is created when the sketch starts. Help: 5.1.5 (Canvas: new Canvas(w, h))

requirements.title: Create at least 2 sprites
requirements.description: Two sprites exist in the sketch. Help: 5.1.6 (Sprite: new Sprite(x, y, w, h) + .color)

requirements.title: Horizontal keyboard input
requirements.description: The left or right key (`'a'`, `'d'`, `'left'` or `'right'`) moves the player horizontally each frame, in draw() or in a function of your own (not setup(), which runs once). Help: 5.1.14 (Key names: WASD and the arrow keys)

requirements.title: Vertical keyboard input
requirements.description: The up or down key (`'w'`, `'s'`, `'up'` or `'down'`) moves the player vertically each frame, in draw() or in a function of your own (not setup(), which runs once). Help: 5.1.14 (Key names: WASD and the arrow keys)

requirements.title: Velocity resets to zero
requirements.description: The player stops when no movement key is held: an else that sets its vel.x or vel.y to 0, or setting it to 0 at the top of draw() before the key checks. Help: 5.1.17 (The else-to-zero rule)

requirements.title: Automatic motion for the mover
requirements.description: The mover (any name, not the sprite the keys drive) moves on its own, with no key held: worked out from frameCount, nudged a little every frame (the way 5.1.9 nudged the player), or given a velocity or a rotationSpeed. Help: 5.1.22 (Moving on its own: frameCount and sin())
requirements.hint: Run it and keep your hands off the keys. If the mover sits still, nothing changes its position or rotation every frame.

requirements.title: On-screen text label
requirements.description: A text label is drawn on the canvas each frame, in draw() or in a function of your own (not setup(), which runs once). Help: 5.1.21 (Words on the canvas: text())

requirements.title: Clear the background each frame
requirements.description: Previous frames don't stack up. Help: 5.1.9 (background(color) wipe rule)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch (p5-style JavaScript with a physics world) for the lab "5.1.23 Sprite Playground". The task they were given: Make a canvas (any size from 300 by 300 to 800 by 600) and two sprites: player, which the keys control, and mover, which moves on its own. In draw(): paint the background every frame; move the player with kb.pressing and WASD or the arrow keys by setting its velocity, with an else that sets the velocity back to 0 when no key is held; make the mover move on its own with no key held, for example worked out from frameCount (swing back and forth, orbit or spin), nudged a little every frame, or given a velocity; and draw a text label on the canvas with fill(), textSize() and text(). What the starter file already had: `let player, mover;` at the top, then an empty setup() and an empty draw() holding only step comments. A file with nothing but those comments meets none of the criteria. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do when the sketch runs. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, if / else chains or ternaries, helper functions, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment or inside a string never runs, so a line the student only wrote in a comment does not count. moSHion facts that matter here: setup() runs once and draw() runs on every frame (update(), if the student writes one, also runs every frame). frameCount is the number of frames since the sketch started, so anything worked out from it changes every frame; sin() and cos() of a small number times frameCount swing between -1 and 1. kb.pressing(key) is true on every frame the key is held. vel.x and vel.y are speed in pixels per frame, and y grows downward. text(words, x, y) draws words on the canvas; fill() sets their colour and textSize() their size. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise. Write for a 14-year-old reader: short sentences and plain, everyday words.

rubric.title: Create a canvas
rubric.description: new Canvas(...) is called when the sketch starts, normally in setup(). Any size counts; the step suggests 300 by 300 up to 800 by 600, and a size a little outside that is close enough. Help: 5.1.5 (Canvas: new Canvas(w, h))

rubric.title: Create at least 2 sprites
rubric.description: Two or more sprites are made with new Sprite(...), normally in setup(): one for the player and one for the mover. Any names, positions and sizes count. Help: 5.1.6 (Sprite: new Sprite(x, y, w, h) + .color)

rubric.title: Horizontal keyboard input
rubric.description: In draw() (or update(), or a function of the student's called from there), a left or right key is read with kb.pressing(...) ('a', 'd', 'left', 'right' or another spelling of the arrow keys) and moves the player sideways. Help: 5.1.14 (Key names: WASD and the arrow keys)

rubric.title: Vertical keyboard input
rubric.description: In draw() (or update(), or a function of the student's called from there), an up or down key is read with kb.pressing(...) ('w', 's', 'up', 'down' or another spelling of the arrow keys) and moves the player up or down. Help: 5.1.14 (Key names: WASD and the arrow keys)

rubric.title: Velocity resets to zero
rubric.description: When no movement key is held, the player's vel.x or vel.y (one or both) is set back to 0, so the player stops. An else at the end of the key chain is the course's shape (with or without braces); any other way that sets it to 0 when no key is held also counts, such as setting it to 0 at the top of draw() before the key checks, or a ternary that ends in 0. Help: 5.1.17 (The else-to-zero rule)

rubric.title: Automatic motion for the mover
rubric.description: The mover (whatever the student named it) changes every frame with no key held. Any honest way counts: its x, y or rotation worked out from frameCount (with or without sin() or cos()); adding a little to its x, y or rotation every frame in draw() or a function draw() calls (written longhand, with +=, or with ++); or giving it a velocity or rotationSpeed that nothing stops. The thing that changes must be a sprite, not only a label: frameCount shown in text() while the mover sits still is not met. A mover that only moves while a key is held, that never moves, or a key-driven player that spins while the mover sits still, is not met. Help: 5.1.22 (Moving on its own: frameCount and sin())

rubric.title: On-screen text label
rubric.description: text(...) is called inside draw() (or a function of the student's that draw() calls) with any words or value, so a label shows on the canvas. fill() and textSize() help it show but are not needed for this card. A text() call only in setup() is wiped by the next background(), so it is not met. Help: 5.1.21 (Words on the canvas: text())

rubric.title: Clear the background each frame
rubric.description: background(...) is called inside draw(), with any colour, so previous frames do not stack up. Help: 5.1.9 (background(color) wipe rule)
